subsystems.name: Sensor array
subsystems.role: picks up the brain's tiny electric fields from outside the head.
parts: fixed headset geometry for repeatable placement

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: lifts microvolt-scale signals above background noise.

subsystems.name: Feature extractor
subsystems.role: turns the raw waveform into a small set of numbers that are stable for one person and differ between people.

subsystems.name: Template store
subsystems.role: holds each enrolled person's reference pattern.

subsystems.name: Matcher
subsystems.role: compares a live recording with the stored template and accepts or rejects.
parts: decision threshold tuned for false accept and false reject rates

subsystems.name: Liveness check
subsystems.role: blocks replay of a recorded or synthesised signal.

buildSteps.title: Pick the recording modality
buildSteps.detail: Scalp EEG is the only practical non-invasive option; it is weak (tens of microvolts) and smeared by skull and scalp, so some work adds fNIRS or MEG-like sensing for robustness.

buildSteps.title: Design the headset
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes are fixed in a repeatable layout so the same positions are used every session, using dry contacts to avoid conductive gel.

buildSteps.title: Collect enrolment data
buildSteps.detail: A person is recorded across several sessions and days, at rest and while performing simple tasks, to capture natural variation rather than one lucky recording.

buildSteps.title: Select stable features
buildSteps.detail: Candidate features are ranked by high variance between people and low variance within one person over time; unstable ones are discarded.

buildSteps.title: Train the matcher
buildSteps.detail: A statistical or machine-learning model is fitted, and its threshold is set to meet a target error rate rather than to maximise headline accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Add liveness
buildSteps.detail: Challenge-response tasks and signal-timing checks are added so a stored recording cannot be replayed into the sensor.

buildSteps.title: Protect the template
buildSteps.detail: The stored pattern is encrypted and, where possible, kept on a secure element in the reader instead of a central database.

buildSteps.title: Validate in the field
buildSteps.detail: Tests span hair types, sweat, caffeine, sleep loss, ageing and electrode drift, because these are what break brain-signal biometrics in practice.

prerequisites.why: gel electrodes give better signal but are unusable for daily access control.
resting-state brain activity does differ between people, but within-person variability across days is large, which is the core obstacle.
unlike a fingerprint, an electrical signal can be recorded and replayed, so liveness must be designed in from the start.
feature extraction and matching must run in the reader, not in the cloud, for privacy and latency.
revocable, encrypted templates are needed because a leaked neural pattern cannot be reissued.

pathway.milestone: laboratory studies using research-grade EEG headsets, mostly short single sessions
pathway.unlocks: proof that some brain-activity features are individual enough to classify.

pathway.milestone: multi-session trials with standard datasets and published liveness tests
pathway.unlocks: a realistic picture of how much accuracy survives weeks and months.

pathway.milestone: deployment as a secondary factor where a slow, deliberate check is acceptable, such as high-security entry
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on usability and spoof resistance.

pathway.milestone: unobtrusive sensing built into a headset or chair
pathway.unlocks: possible everyday use, though it is more likely to remain a complement to face or fingerprint than a replacement.
